Prealgebra · Lesson 5.2

Decimal Arithmetic

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Decimal arithmetic is not new arithmetic. Every digit still sits in a place worth ten times the place to its right, and a decimal is just a fraction over a power of ten. The only genuinely new job is bookkeeping, knowing exactly where the point belongs in the answer. Adding, multiplying, and dividing each handle that job differently, so we will work through all three.

Problem
A runner covers 1.71.7 km then 0.450.45 km. Stack the numbers with decimal points aligned, pad 1.71.7 to 1.701.70, and add column by column. What is 1.7+0.451.7+0.45 in km?
Show a hint
  • Write the two numbers one above the other with the decimal points lined up. Since 1.71.7 has no hundredths digit, fill that empty spot with a trailing zero so it reads 1.701.70, which is the same value.
  • Add the columns from the right. Hundredths give 0+5=50+5=5, tenths give 7+4=117+4=11 so write 11 and carry 11, and ones give 1+0+1=21+0+1=2. Bring the decimal point straight down.
Show the full solution
Stack the numbers with the points aligned and pad 1.71.7 to 1.701.70 so both show a hundredths digit. 1.70+ 0.452.151.70+0.452.15​​ Adding right to left, hundredths give 0+5=50+5=5, tenths give 7+4=117+4=11 so write 11 and carry 11, and ones give 1+0+1=21+0+1=2. The point drops straight down. The runner covers 2.152.15​ km.
Problem
A café lists a sandwich at 12.512.5 dollars and a cookie at 0.450.45 dollars. Align the decimal points, pad 12.512.5 to 12.5012.50, and add. What is the correct total?
Show a hint
  • A decimal place only means something next to its neighbors. The tenths digit must sit above the tenths digit, and hundredths above hundredths. Stack the numbers so the two decimal points fall in one straight vertical line, not so the last digits line up.
  • Write 12.5012.50 on top and 0.450.45 underneath with the points aligned. Add the hundredths, 0+5=50+5=5. Add the tenths, 5+4=95+4=9. Bring down the 1212 and drop the point straight down.
Show the full solution
Pad 12.512.5 to 12.5012.50 so both numbers show two decimal places, then stack them with the points in one vertical line. 12.50+  0.4512.9512.50+0.4512.95​​ The hundredths give 0+5=50+5=5, the tenths give 5+4=95+4=9, and the 1212 comes straight down. The total is 12.9512.95​ dollars. Line up the right edges instead and the 55 tenths sits above the 55 hundredths, adding digits of different sizes and inflating a few cents into a few dollars.
Problem
A bottle holds 5.25.2 litres. After pouring, 3.653.65 litres remain. Line up the decimal points and subtract. How many litres were poured out?
Show a hint
  • Write 5.25.2 as 5.205.20 first. Now both numbers have a tenths digit and a hundredths digit, so every column has something to subtract.
  • In the hundredths column 0−50−5 needs a borrow, so take 11 tenth, making it 10−5=510−5=5. In the tenths column the 22 became 11, so 1−61−6 borrows again, giving 11−6=511−6=5. In the ones column 4−3=14−3=1. Read it off with the point in place.
Show the full solution
Pad 5.25.2 to 5.205.20 and stack it over 3.653.65 with the points aligned. In the hundredths column, borrow 11 tenth to get 10−5=510−5=5. That leaves 11 in the tenths, so borrow 11 one to get 11−6=511−6=5. The ones column is then 4−3=14−3=1. Bringing the point straight down gives 1.551.55​ litres. Checking it, 3.65+1.55=5.203.65+1.55=5.20, the full bottle again.
Key idea
Adding and subtracting decimals. Line up the decimal points so tenths sit over tenths and hundredths over hundredths, since the point marks where the ones place stops. Pad a shorter number with trailing zeros, which is allowed because a zero on the end changes nothing. Then add or subtract column by column as usual, and the point of the answer goes straight down under the points above. Line up the right edges instead and you stack tenths on hundredths, which gives the wrong answer.
Problem
Your gut might say 0.3×0.2=0.60.3×0.2=0.6. Resist it and compute 310×210103​×102​ instead. What is 0.3×0.20.3×0.2?
Show a hint
  • Turn each decimal into a fraction over ten. You are multiplying 310103​ by 210102​, so multiply the tops together and the bottoms together.
  • The tops give 3×2=63×2=6 and the bottoms give 10×10=10010×10=100, so you have 61001006​. A denominator of 100100 means two digits after the point, and you need a leading zero to fill the empty tenths place.
Show the full solution
Write each decimal as a fraction over ten and multiply across, 310×210=3×210×10=6100103​×102​=10×103×2​=1006​. A denominator of 100100 puts the digits two places past the point, so the answer is 0.060.06 and not 0.60.6. So 0.3×0.2=0.060.3×0.2=0.06​. Taking a fraction of a fraction always lands below both factors, which is why the product is smaller than 0.30.3 and 0.20.2.
Problem
A herb bed measures 0.60.6 m by 0.70.7 m. Write 0.6=6100.6=106​, 0.7=7100.7=107​, multiply as fractions, and read off the decimal area. What is 0.6×0.70.6×0.7 in square metres?
Show a hint
  • You already did the hard part above. The fractions multiplied to 4210010042​, so now just turn that back into a decimal.
  • 4210010042​ is forty-two hundredths. Hundredths live two places after the point, so write 4242 and slide the point so the last digit lands in the second place: 0.420.42.
Show the full solution
Write the decimals as fractions and multiply across, 610×710=6×710×10=42100106​×107​=10×106×7​=10042​. A denominator of 100100 is the hundredths place, so that reads as forty-two hundredths, and the bed is 0.420.42​ square metres. There is a shortcut hiding in that. The digits gave 6×7=426×7=42, and each factor had one decimal place, so the product carries two.
Problem
Almonds cost 0.250.25 dollars per scoop. You take 77 scoops. Multiply 7×25=1757×25=175, then place the decimal point. What do you owe in dollars?
Show a hint
  • A whole number does not break the rule, it just brings zero decimal places to the table. Start by ignoring the point and multiplying the digits as whole numbers, 7×257×25.
  • You found 7×25=1757×25=175. Now count decimal places in both factors together. The 77 has none and 0.250.25 has two, so the product needs two places. Put the point two digits from the right of 175175.
Show the full solution
Strip the point and multiply the digits like ordinary whole numbers, 7×25=1757×25=175. Now total the decimal places in the two factors. The whole number 77 carries zero places and 0.250.25 carries two, so the product keeps 0+2=20+2=2 places. Placing the point two digits from the right turns 175175 into 1.751.75. A quick gut check, 0.250.25 is a quarter of a dollar, so seven quarters is 1.751.75 dollars, exactly as expected. So 7×0.25=1.757×0.25=1.75​ dollars.
Problem
A recipe needs 0.20.2 of a 0.040.04 gram pinch of saffron. Multiply: 4×2=84×2=8, count three total decimal places, and place the point. How many grams is that?
Show a hint
  • Multiply as whole numbers first, 4×2=84×2=8, then count the decimal places in both factors. Two places plus one place means the answer needs three places total.
  • You have the digit 88 but it must sit three places after the point. Fill the first two places after the point with zeros and put the 88 in the third, the thousandths spot.
Show the full solution
Ignore the points and multiply the digits, 4×2=84×2=8. Then count places. 0.040.04 has two and 0.20.2 has one, so the product needs 2+1=32+1=3. Two zeros push the 88 out to the thousandths spot, so the recipe uses 0.0080.008​ grams. The fractions agree, since 4100×210=81,0001004​×102​=1,0008​ and thousandths is exactly that third place.
Key idea
Multiplying decimals. Ignore the points and multiply the digits like plain whole numbers, then place the point by counting. Add up how many decimal places the two factors have between them, and the product has exactly that many. That works because each factor is a whole number over a power of ten, so the denominators multiply and the places add. If the whole-number product is too short to reach that far, write zeros in front until the last digit sits in the right place, the way eight thousandths must be 0.0080.008 and not 0.80.8. For 0.3×0.20.3×0.2, the digits give 66 and the factors have two decimal places between them, so the answer is 0.060.06.
Key idea
Multiplying by a number less than one gives a smaller result. You are taking only part of what you started with, so 0.3×0.20.3×0.2 is less than both 0.30.3 and 0.20.2, and equals 0.060.06. Do not judge size by length. 0.060.06 has more digits than 0.60.6 yet is ten times smaller, because size is set by the leftmost place, not by the digit count.
Fun fact
The US chose base-ten money in 1792, dividing the dollar into 100 cents. Britain held out until 1971, when it replaced 240 pence per pound with 100 pence, an event called Decimal Day.
Problem
A 4.54.5 m rope is cut into 0.50.5 m pieces. Write 4.5÷0.54.5÷0.5 as 4.50.50.54.5​, multiply top and bottom by 1010 to get 455545​, then divide. How many pieces?
Show a hint
  • The divisor is 0.50.5, which has one decimal place. Slide the point one place to the right in both numbers so the divisor becomes a whole number. What do 4.54.5 and 0.50.5 turn into?
  • Sliding both points one place gives 45÷545÷5. Now it is plain whole-number division, and 55 goes into 4545 exactly how many times?
Show the full solution
Write the division as 4.50.50.54.5​ and multiply the top and bottom by 1010, which slides each point one place right and gives 455545​. Since 5×9=455×9=45, the rope makes 99​ pieces. Multiplying top and bottom by the same number is multiplying by 11, so the slide cannot change the value.
Key idea
Dividing by a decimal. Move the decimal point in both numbers the same number of places to the right, just enough to make the divisor a whole number, then divide as usual. Moving both points multiplies the numerator and denominator by the same power of ten, so the fraction stays equivalent and the quotient does not change. To add and subtract, line up the points. To multiply, count the places. To divide, move the point.
Problem
Find 1.44÷1.21.44÷1.2. Write it as 1.441.21.21.44​, multiply top and bottom by 1010 to clear the divisor, then divide. What is the quotient?
Show a hint
  • Multiply both 1.441.44 and 1.21.2 by 1010 so the divisor turns whole. That leaves you with 14.4÷1214.4÷12, which has the same value but is much friendlier.
  • Divide 14.414.4 by 1212. Since 1212 goes into 1414 once with 2.42.4 left, and 1212 goes into 2.42.4 exactly 0.20.2 times, the quotient is 1.21.2. Bring the decimal point straight up and you land on 1.21.2.
Show the full solution
Multiply the top and bottom of 1.441.21.21.44​ by 1010 to clear the divisor, which turns the problem into 14.4÷1214.4÷12. Twelve fits into 1414 once, leaving 2.42.4, and twelve fits into 2.42.4 exactly 0.20.2 times, so 1.44÷1.2=1.21.44÷1.2=1.2​. Check it by multiplying back, since 1.2×1.2=1.441.2×1.2=1.44.
Problem
A maker has 33 spools of 1.21.2 m wire each and uses 2.752.75 m. Find the total wire on hand, then subtract what is used. How many metres are left?
Show a hint
  • Two clean steps. Step one is a whole number times a decimal, so multiply 3×1.23×1.2 to get the total length on hand. Step two is a subtraction, the total minus the 2.752.75 m used.
  • Multiply 3×12=363×12=36, and since 1.21.2 has one decimal place the total carries one place too, giving 3.63.6 m. Now line up the points and subtract 3.60−2.753.60−2.75, padding 3.63.6 to 3.603.60 so both numbers show hundredths.
Show the full solution
Three spools of 1.21.2 m each is 3×1.23×1.2. The digits give 3×12=363×12=36, and 1.21.2 carries one decimal place, so there is 3.63.6 m on hand. Pad that to 3.603.60, line up the points, and subtract what the build uses. 3.60−2.75=0.853.60−2.75=0.85 That leaves 0.850.85​ m of wire.

Practice these ideas

Practice
Two reef stretches measure 4.34.3 m and 5.65.6 m. Line up the decimal points and add. What is 4.3+5.64.3+5.6?
Show the solution
Both numbers already show one decimal place, so stack them with the points aligned and add. The tenths give 3+6=93+6=9 and the ones give 4+5=94+5=9, with the point dropping straight down. The two stretches total 9.99.9​ meters.
Practice
A stack holds 7.27.2 liters. You pour out 3.853.85 liters. Pad 7.27.2 to 7.207.20 and subtract. How many liters remain?
Show the solution
Pad 7.27.2 to 7.207.20 so both numbers show hundredths, then line up the points and subtract from the right. The hundredths borrow to give 10−5=510−5=5. The tenths are now 11, so borrow again for 11−8=311−8=3. The ones give 6−3=36−3=3. Bringing the point down leaves 3.353.35​ liters.
Practice
A drone starts with 66 units of battery and the trip uses 2.352.35 units. Write 66 as 6.006.00 and subtract. How many units remain?
Show the solution
Write 66 as 6.006.00, the same value with two decimal places, and stack it over 2.352.35 with the points aligned. 6.00− 2.353.656.00−2.353.65​​ The hundredths borrow to give 10−5=510−5=5, the tenths become 9−3=69−3=6 as the borrow cascades, and the ones give 5−2=35−2=3. So 3.653.65​ units of charge are left. Checking it, 2.35+3.65=6.002.35+3.65=6.00, a full battery again.
Practice
A square sticker measures 0.80.8 cm by 0.40.4 cm. Multiply the digits, count two total decimal places, and place the point. What is the area?
Show the solution
Ignore the decimal points and multiply the digits like whole numbers, 8×4=328×4=32. Then count the decimal places in the factors, one in 0.80.8 and one in 0.40.4, which makes two in all. Giving 3232 two decimal places turns it into 0.320.32​.
Practice
Fog covers 0.60.6 of a window. By noon it blocks only 0.50.5 of that area. What fraction of the whole window is still fogged? Give your answer as a decimal.
Show the solution
Half of the fogged area means 0.5×0.60.5×0.6. The digits give 5×6=305×6=30, and each factor has one decimal place, so the product needs two, giving 0.300.30​ of the window. It landed below both 0.50.5 and 0.60.6, which is what taking a part of a part always does.
Practice
A vial holds 2.52.5 grams of saffron. A recipe uses 0.40.4 of the vial. What is 2.5×0.42.5×0.4 in grams?
Show the solution
Set the points aside and multiply like whole numbers, 25×4=10025×4=100. There is one decimal place in 2.52.5 and one in 0.40.4, so the product needs two, and counting two spots from the right of 100100 gives 1.001.00. Trailing zeros after the point add nothing, so the recipe uses 11​ gram. Two numbers that both carry decimals can still multiply to a clean whole number, when the places fill in exactly.
Practice
A reading is 0.030.03 grams. Another mass is 0.30.3 of that first amount. What is 0.03×0.30.03×0.3?
Show the solution
Start with the digits and forget the decimals. Multiplying 3×33×3 gives 99. Now count how many decimal places the factors have. The number 0.030.03 has two places and 0.30.3 has one place, for a total of three. The product must therefore have three decimal places. Writing 99 with three places means filling in zeros, so 99 sits in the thousandths spot as 0.0090.009. 0.0090.009​
Practice
Slide both numbers in 7.2÷0.97.2÷0.9 one place right to make the divisor whole. What is 7.2÷0.97.2÷0.9?
Show the solution
Sliding both numbers one place to the right means multiplying each by 1010, and doing the same thing to both keeps the quotient the same. So 7.2÷0.97.2÷0.9 becomes 72÷972÷9. Now the divisor is a whole number and the work is easy. Since 9×8=729×8=72, we get 72÷9=872÷9=8. Therefore 7.2÷0.9=87.2÷0.9=8​.
Practice
A ribbon is 2.562.56 m long. A pattern piece needs 1.61.6 m. How many times as long as one strip is the whole ribbon? Find 2.56÷1.62.56÷1.6.
Show the solution
Start by making the divisor whole. Slide both points one place to the right, so 2.562.56 becomes 25.625.6 and 1.61.6 becomes 1616. The quotient does not change, so 2.56÷1.6=25.6÷162.56÷1.6=25.6÷16. Now divide. 1616 goes into 2525 once, leaving 99. Bring down the 66 to make 9696, and 16×6=9616×6=96, so the next digit is 66. Keeping the decimal point in place gives 1.61.6. Check by multiplying back, 1.6×1.6=2.561.6×1.6=2.56, which matches the ribbon. So the ribbon is 1.61.6​ times as long as one strip.
Practice
Add 0.080.08 mm and 0.90.9 mm. Pad the shorter number so both show two decimal places, then add. What is 0.08+0.90.08+0.9?
Show the solution
Pad 0.90.9 to 0.900.90 and line up the points. The hundredths give 8+0=88+0=8 and the tenths give 0+9=90+9=9. 0.08+0.90=0.980.08+0.90=0.98 The total is 0.980.98​ mm. The inner zero in 0.080.08 is doing real work, since it holds the 88 in the hundredths place instead of letting it drift up to the tenths.
Practice
A kit needs half of a 1.41.4 m wire length. Multiply 1.4×0.51.4×0.5. Count decimal places and place the point. What is the result?
Show the solution
Ignore the points and multiply the digits, 14×5=7014×5=70. There is one decimal place in 1.41.4 and one in 0.50.5, so the answer needs two, giving 1.4×0.5=0.701.4×0.5=0.70​ m. That matches taking half of 1.41.4.
Practice
You buy 44 jars of jam at 0.850.85 dollars each and pay with a 55 dollar bill. Find the total cost, then subtract from 55. How much change do you get?
Show the solution
Start with the cost of the jam. Multiply 4×0.854×0.85. Ignoring the point for a moment, 4×85=3404×85=340. The factor 0.850.85 has two digits after the point, so the product does too, giving 4×0.85=3.404×0.85=3.40. Now find the change. Write the 55 dollar bill as 5.005.00 so the points line up, then subtract. 5.00−3.40=1.605.00−3.40=1.60. So your change is 1.601.60​ dollars.
